source.check: returned unopposed: the only candidate nominated (Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1924: only Gilford had a possible contest)

note: Triennial election of Down County Council on the 20 county electoral divisions; nominations received by R. J. Dickson, returning officer, at Downpatrick on 7 May 1924. Seventeen divisions were returned unopposed and no one was nominated for Castlewellan or Warrenpoint; the only poll was in Gilford on Thursday 5 June 1924, counted at the County Courthouse, Downpatrick, the next day (Belfast News-Letter, 8 May and 7 June 1924). The nominations list prints no party labels, so none are given. Castlewellan and Warrenpoint, where the Nationalists made no nomination, had no retiring member to be deemed re-elected in the new single-member divisions, so the seats fell to the council to fill as casual vacancies: at the new council's first meeting (17 June 1924) 'the question of nominating members for the vacant divisions of Castlewellan and Warrenpoint' was left in the chairman's hands (Frontier Sentinel, 21 June 1924, p. 7). No co-option to either seat was traced; a co-option would not be an election (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
